title: LAVA: Lifetime-Aware VM Allocation with Learned Distributions and Adaptation to Mispredictions
problem: VM scheduling in hyperscale cloud data centers is NP-hard with incomplete lifetime information; one-shot lifetime predictions accumulate mispredictions over time, causing host fragmentation and wasted capacity.
motivation: 88% of VMs live less than 1 hour but 98% of core-hours are consumed by longer-lived VMs. One-shot prediction tools like LA-Binary degrade rapidly with prediction errors. Repredicting remaining lifetime using observed uptime enables adaptive correction of mispredictions and fundamentally better scheduling.
method: LAVA: three lifetime-aware algorithms using distribution-based VM lifetime prediction. ML model: GBDT trained on VM features (zone, family, shape, SSD, project metadata) to predict E(Tr|Tu) — conditional expected remaining lifetime given observed uptime. Multiple training examples per VM by augmenting with Tu quantiles. Model compiled into Borg scheduler binary (<10us latency, 780x faster than LA-Binary's inference server). Three algorithms: (1) NILAS — non-invasive reprediction tie-breaker using max repredicted exit time of co-scheduled VMs; (2) LAVA — lifetime-class based host state machine (open/recycling) placing shorter-lived VMs in gaps of longer-lived hosts, upgrading/downgrading host lifetime class on mispredictions; (3) LARS — lifetime-guided migration ordering for defragmentation, migrating longest-lived VMs first to let shorter VMs exit naturally.
key_novelty: First production VM scheduler to use distribution-based lifetime reprediction (conditional expectation updated via uptime) and adapt scheduling decisions on misprediction detection, demonstrating that reprediction is theoretically and practically superior to one-shot prediction.
contributions: Distribution-based GBDT lifetime model predicting E(Tr|Tu) at 99% precision/70% recall for 7-day threshold
Theoretical proof that reprediction reduces host requirements by Omega(m) over one-shot prediction
NILAS: non-invasive reprediction-based tie-breaker integrated into existing lexicographic scorer
LAVA: lifetime-class host state machine with adaptive misprediction correction
LARS: lifetime-guided migration ordering reducing live migrations by 4.5%
Fleet-wide production deployment at Google Borg, improving empty hosts 2.3-9.2 pp

metrics.accuracy: 3% stranded compute reduction, 2% stranded memory reduction; 2.3-9.2 pp increase in empty hosts; 4.5% reduction in VM migrations
metrics.other: Model latency <10us (780x faster than LA-Binary); fleet-wide production deployment

limitations: Focuses on bin-packing timing; does not model FLOPS utilization or energy directly
Model requires periodic retraining (monthly) as workload distributions shift
LAVA's invasive scoring may conflict with other high-priority business metrics in some pools
